generation_specification.overview: Reusable generation recipe for the mountain/climber schema. Two tables: mountain (parent) and climber (child, FK Mountain_ID -> mountain.Mountain_ID). Generation order: mountain first, then climber. Each instance starts as a copy of the compact database (7 mountain rows, 8 climber rows) and appends generated rows; compact rows are never deleted or changed. table_sizes_per_instance counts GENERATED rows only (compact rows are additional). All rules describe non-NULL values only; NULLs are planted per null_targets and never replaced.

generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at max(compact PK)+1, unique per table, never NULL; never collide with compact rows.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Sample from the FINAL parent table's primary-key values (compact + generated, after dedupe/truncation); with probability 0.20 emit NULL (only where the column is nullable).
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from a small pool of realistic short strings; allow near-duplicate variants (case, spacing, punctuation) with probability 0.2; NULL with probability equal to the compact share for that column (at least one NULL row per nullable column).
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Sample from a pool of realistic proper names; allow near-duplicate variants with probability 0.2; NULL with probability equal to the compact share for that column.
generic_sampling_rules.text_country: Sample from a fixed country pool; allow duplicates across rows (20-50% duplicate share); NULL with probability equal to the compact share for that column.
generic_sampling_rules.real_positive: Sample a positive real number within the column's range rule; include boundary values at each listed literal and one step on each side; clamp to satisfy the semantic range rule; NULL with probability equal to the compact share for that column.
generic_sampling_rules.real_ranked: Sample a positive real number; force ties at the listed LIMIT ranks by repeating the value at each forced rank; NULL with probability equal to the compact share for that column.
generic_sampling_rules.text_time: Sample a race-time string of the form H:MM.SS.S; allow duplicates (20-50% duplicate share); NULL with probability equal to the compact share for that column.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: 0.8 of values are fresh samples; 0.2 are near-variants or duplicates of existing values. The reuse share is applied deterministically per column (not via a per-instance coin flip); no column-type override may set the reuse share to 0.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share_default: Per (table, column) NULL share = count(NULLs)/count(rows) in the compact database; spec NULL_SHARE overrides only where stated (climber.Mountain_ID = 0.20). At least one NULL row per nullable column per instance, even when the compact share is 0.

supporting_evidence.mountain.Country: Rows: Tanzania, Kenya, DR Congo Uganda, Uganda.
supporting_evidence.climber.Country: Rows: West Germany, Switzerland, United Kingdom.

uncertainty: No formula links climber.Points to climber.Time or to mountain.Height; Points appears to be a rank-based score, not a computed column.
climber.Mountain_ID is nullable in the schema; the original sample has no NULLs but the atomic summary requires a 5-30% NULL share (spec uses 0.20).
mountain.Country and mountain.Range enum values are taken from the original sample; no CHECK constraint confirms them. They are kept as soft generation hints, not asserted invariants.
The 'Prominence <= Height' rule holds on all shown rows but is a physical plausibility rule, not a declared constraint; kept as a soft hint.

climber.Points tie_at_rank [10,1000] from the atomic summary: rank 1000 is not representable at the declared generated size (climber=14); the spec keeps rank 1 and rank 10 (the largest representable rank) and drops rank 1000. This is consistent with table_sizes_per_instance.climber = 14.

climber.Climber_ID unmatched_join_rows target (joins_with mountain.Mountain_ID, child_rows_with_null_fk false) is not representable: Climber_ID is a primary key and cannot be NULL, and it is not a foreign key to mountain. The target is documented here as not implemented.
table_sizes_per_instance counts generated rows only; compact rows (7 mountain, 8 climber) are copied in addition and never modified.
Unmatched-parent planting must respect the climber.Mountain_ID NULL share budget (0.20); it is applied within the null-share step, not as an extra post-hoc NULL.
